title: EPA Rejects Chlorpyrifos Ban
description_short: EPA denied petitions to ban the pesticide chlorpyrifos, keeping the chemical on the market despite health concerns.

title: Trump Commutes Remaining Confinement Term of Rashella Reed
description_short: Trump Commutes Remaining Confinement Term of Rashella Reed
description_medium: DOJ's October 21, 2020 clemency warrant says Trump commuted the remainder of Rashella Reed's confinement sentence to time served and directed her immediate release from home confinement. It left her unpaid restitution balance of $8,254,239.46, three-year supervised release and its conditions, and the other sentence components intact. The warrant identifies her Georgia wire-fraud and money-laundering conspiracy case.
description_long: The Department of Justice's October 21, 2020 executive clemency warrant identifies Rashella Reed as convicted in the Southern District of Georgia of wire-fraud conspiracy and money-laundering conspiracy. It records a 168-month prison sentence, three years of supervised release, and $8,254,239.46 in restitution imposed on November 6, 2013. The warrant says Reed had been in federal custody since December 2013 and was moved to home confinement in June 2020, with a projected release date of November 7, 2025. President Donald Trump commuted the remainder of her confinement sentence to time served. The warrant expressly left the unpaid restitution balance, supervised-release term and conditions, and all other sentence components in effect, while directing the Bureau of Prisons to release her from home confinement immediately. DOJ's clemency table lists her as “Rashella Reed” under the October 21, 2020 section; the signed warrant confirms that the earlier title's middle initial was not part of the official document. These records establish the relief and its limits, but do not state why Reed was selected for clemency.
notes: The DOJ commutations table lists Rashella Reed under October 21, 2020, with her Southern District of Georgia case, 168-month sentence, three years' supervised release, $8,254,239.46 restitution, and wire-fraud/money-laundering conspiracy offenses. The table's directly linked executive grant states the remaining confinement was commuted to time served, restitution and supervised release remained intact, and BOP was directed to release her from home confinement. It uses “Rashella Reed” without the middle initial in the earlier title.

title: Pardons Glen Moss
description_short: Trump granted a presidential pardon to Glen Moss as part of a clemency list.
description_medium: DOJ lists Glen Moss under its January 19, 2021 pardons and associates him with cases in Connecticut and South Carolina. The table gives probation, fine, home-confinement, and restitution terms for the separate cases. A directly linked executive grant includes “Glen S. Moss” among recipients of full and unconditional pardons, but says the covered offenses were individually enumerated elsewhere and does not identify them; the case-specific scope remains unresolved.
description_long: The Justice Department's pardon table places Glen Moss in the January 19, 2021 section and lists two federal case histories: a District of Connecticut matter involving payment to a non-licensed physician and attempted tax evasion, and a District of South Carolina mail-fraud case. It records three years' probation and a $4,000 fine in the Connecticut case, conditioned on cooperating with the IRS over $100,000 in unpaid taxes, and five years' probation, six months' home confinement, and $412,000 restitution in the South Carolina case. The linked executive grant says President Trump issued full and unconditional pardons to a group that includes “Glen S. Moss,” for offenses individually enumerated and presented for consideration. That group document does not list Moss's offenses or say whether both case histories were included. It confirms a pardon and date but cannot resolve which conviction or obligations it covered. The case-specific enumeration or an individual warrant remains necessary; the documents do not explain the reason for the pardon.
